no_retrieval.title: No retrieval
no_retrieval.note: A simple question is answered by the language model alone, without consulting any external source.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The language model answers the question with what the chosen route retrieved, or with nothing retrieved.

omitted.D2: The paper does not describe how retrieved documents are selected: the multi-step route is borrowed whole from another work.

design.title: Per-agent memory design
design.note: When an agent connects, the system generates a memory design from a description of its purpose: what to extract and how to store, retrieve and compact it. This design governs every later step.

resolve.title: Entity resolution
resolve.note: Different surface forms of one name are linked to one canonical entity, so facts about it are not scattered.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The model receives the retrieved items, the compacted conversation and the recent turns.

graph.title: Graph construction
graph.note: The texts are cut into chunks of a set length; a language model extracts the entities and relations of each chunk, and the pieces are merged into one graph.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The language model writes the answer from the most relevant reports; whatever exceeds the text limit is cut off.

synthesis.title: Synthesizing training data
synthesis.note: A language model prompted with examples solves questions from existing datasets, alternating reasoning and retrieval. Its moves are recorded as training examples.

filtering.title: Data filtering
filtering.note: At each step a query whose documents contain part of the answer is preferred; an example is kept only if its final answer matches the reference.

retrieval.title: Document retrieval
retrieval.note: The query written by the model is sent to the retriever, and the retrieved documents go back to the model.

answer.title: Final answer
answer.note: Once the model decides it knows enough, it stops writing queries and outputs the answer.

input.title: Text in 100+ languages
input.note: The model accepts text in more than a hundred languages, from a short sentence to a document of 8192 tokens.

encode.title: Single encoder pass
encode.note: One model produces all three kinds of text representation in a single pass.

sparse.title: Lexical weights
sparse.note: Each word of the text gets a weight, as in BM25, and texts are compared by the words they share.

colbert.title: Multi-vector (ColBERT)
colbert.note: The text is represented by many vectors, and similarity is computed by late interaction, as in ColBERT.

score.title: Weighted score sum
score.note: The scores of the three kinds of matching are added up with weights set by the user.

causal.title: Causal path discovery
causal.note: A language model keeps only the causal links among the collected nodes and edges and builds a causal graph from them.

summary.title: Causal summary
summary.note: The summary traces the key causal paths and drops material that is similar in meaning but not causally related.

casebase.title: Case base
casebase.note: Each case consists of a question, an answer and a supporting passage from a legal document.

retrieval.title: Case retrieval
retrieval.note: The question is compared with the questions, passages and entities of the cases. The similarities are added up with weights, and the best few cases are taken.

context.title: Context assembly
context.note: The prompt receives either the supporting passage alone or the whole case.

sft.title: Instruction tuning
sft.note: The language model is fine-tuned to follow instructions and hold a conversation on a blend of instruction and dialogue datasets.

context_tuning.title: Context-enhanced tuning
context_tuning.note: The model learns to answer in conversation from a given text and to say so plainly when the text holds no answer.

dialogue.title: Dialogue and question
dialogue.note: The retriever receives the whole previous conversation together with the current question, with no rewriting of the question.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The top retrieved passages (five long ones or twenty short ones, depending on the dataset) go to the tuned model, which answers the question.

index.title: Vector index
index.note: All document vectors are stored in advance in a fast search library, and each vector remembers its document.

q_enc.title: Query encoding
q_enc.note: The query is padded with special blank tokens to a fixed length, and the same model builds a vector for each token.

rescore.title: Exact rescoring
rescore.note: For each query vector the highest similarity to the document vectors is taken, and these values are summed.

store.title: Vector store
store.note: For every page a set of vectors, one per image patch, is stored in advance.

q_enc.title: Query encoding
q_enc.note: The same model builds a vector for each token of the query.

score.title: Page scoring
score.note: For each query vector the highest similarity to the page vectors is taken, and these values are summed.

chunks.title: Splitting into chunks
chunks.note: Documents are cut into small chunks, usually no more than a few hundred tokens.

bm25.title: Word index
bm25.note: The same chunk with its context also goes into a word-match (BM25) index.

search.title: Chunk search
search.note: The closest chunks are looked up in both indexes, and the lists are merged.

retrieval.title: Initial retrieval
retrieval.note: An ordinary retriever finds about ten documents for the question in the system's own collection.

web.title: Web search
web.note: The pages found on the web are cut into strips and filtered by the same evaluator before they reach the answer.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The language model answers from the selected knowledge: from its own documents, from the web, or from both when the evaluation is unsure.

index.title: Vector index
index.note: Each proposition is turned into a vector by a ready-made encoder and stored in the index.

search.title: Proposition search
search.note: The question is compared with the propositions by their vectors. The authors test four ready-made retrievers.

signature.title: Declaring signatures
signature.note: Instead of prompt text, each step is described by what it takes and what it returns, such as "question -> answer".

modules.title: Modules replace prompts
modules.note: A module builds the prompt from that description, calls the language model and parses its output. Ready-made modules cover step-by-step reasoning and tool use.

program.title: Composing the program
program.note: Modules are joined by ordinary Python code: branches, loops, calls to retrieval.

examples.title: Examples and metric
examples.note: The optimizer receives the program, a few training examples, often with final answers only, and a metric.

bootstrap.title: Bootstrapping examples
bootstrap.note: The program is run on training questions. Traces that pass the metric become demonstrations for each module.

higher.title: Higher-order optimization
higher.note: The compiler may also change the program's control flow, for example run several copies and pick the answer by majority vote.

compiled.title: Compiled program
compiled.note: The result is a new program with selected prompts or a finetuned model.

omitted.B1: The library itself does not reformulate questions: only a program the user writes may generate search queries.

lexidx.title: Keyword index
lexidx.note: A simple table maps each keyword to the ids of the chunks that contain it.

prefilter.title: Keyword prefilter
prefilter.note: Chunks are scored by the share of the question's keywords they contain. Usually thousands of chunks shrink to fewer than fifty.

scoring.title: Hybrid scoring
scoring.note: The remaining chunks are ordered by a weighted sum of vector similarity and keyword share. The paper calls this stage reranking, but no separate reranking model is used.

compress.title: Context compression
compress.note: Sentences in the selected chunks are scored by overlap with the question's keywords and by medical terms, and only the most relevant are kept. The text is not rewritten.

chunks.title: Splitting into fragments
chunks.note: The text collection is split into small fragments.

vectors.title: Vector representations
vectors.note: A vector is computed for every fragment.

clusters.title: Clustering
clusters.note: Similar vectors are grouped into clusters. The cluster centres always stay in the device's memory.

centroid.title: Nearest cluster
centroid.note: The question's vector is compared with the cluster centres, and the closest cluster is chosen.

stored.title: Precomputed vectors
stored.note: For clusters that are slow to compute, the vectors were saved in advance and are simply loaded.

generated.title: On-the-fly generation
generated.note: For the other clusters the vectors are computed at query time. The most expensive ones are kept for later queries.

frames.title: Posed images
frames.note: Each node of the map stores an image with the position and time of capture. These nodes are what the search returns.

descent.title: Top-down descent
descent.note: At every level a language model reads the descriptions and chooses branches, until the descent reaches the nodes of the map. No vectors are compared.

route.title: Path planning
route.note: The shortest path from the robot's current position to the chosen waypoint is found along the links of the map.

pairs.title: Training pairs
pairs.note: Questions are generated automatically from each client's own chunks. Each question with its chunk forms a positive training example.

distill.title: Knowledge distillation
distill.note: The similarities produced by a client's local model are pulled towards those of the server's global model, which evens out differences between the clients' data.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The retrieved chunks are joined to the question, and the client's language model writes the answer.

draft.title: Draft next sentence
draft.note: The language model drafts the next sentence without retrieved documents; only the first sentence follows a search by the question itself.

accept.title: Accept as is
accept.note: If the model is confident about every word of the draft, the draft stays in the answer unchanged.

graphs.title: Existing graphs
graphs.note: The input is graphs of different kinds: a knowledge graph, a document graph, a hierarchy of communities.

unify.title: Conversion to one format
unify.note: Each of these graphs is converted into one format of four layers: attributes, entities with their relations, documents and communities.

encode.title: Text embeddings
encode.note: A ready embedding model encodes the text of every node, the description of every relation and the question itself.

omitted.A2: The method takes ready graphs built by other tools and does not itself split text into fragments.

resolution.title: Linking synonyms
resolution.note: Entities with close embeddings, such as USA and United States of America, are joined by an extra edge.

topents.title: Top entities
topents.note: The entities with the highest relevance scores for the question are taken.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The top documents and the question are given to a language model, which writes the answer.

omitted.A2: Documents are taken whole and are not cut into fragments.

subgraph.title: Question subgraph
subgraph.note: A small subgraph is taken from the large graph: the entities named in the question and their neighbours.

verbalize.title: Paths as text
verbalize.note: Each path is written as a line: question entity, relation, entity, and so on up to the last relation and the answer entity.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: A language model reads the paths and the question and lists the answers. A model with open weights is fine-tuned for this.

split.title: Text splitting
split.note: The long document is split into chunks of limited length without breaking paragraphs.

plan.title: Solution plan
plan.note: The agent breaks the question into steps and decides what information the answer needs.

start.title: Choosing starting nodes
start.note: The agent looks through the key elements of all nodes and picks where to start, guided by the question and the plan.

answer.title: Answer from notes
answer.note: A language model gathers the notes of all agents, settles conflicts by majority vote and writes the answer.

synonyms.title: Linking synonyms
synonyms.note: Similar but not identical names, likely synonyms, are joined by an extra edge when the similarity of their embeddings exceeds a threshold of 0.8.

qnodes.title: Query nodes
qnodes.note: Each question entity is matched to the graph node with the closest embedding.

specificity.title: Node specificity
specificity.note: The weight of each query node is divided by the number of passages it was extracted from, so rare nodes weigh more.

avg.title: Vector averaging
avg.note: The invented documents and the question itself are encoded by the same encoder as the real documents, and the vectors are averaged.

doc_enc.title: Document encoding
doc_enc.note: An encoder trained without labelled examples turns each document into a vector.

search.title: Similarity search
search.note: The average vector is compared with the vectors of all documents by inner product.

first.title: Search by the question
first.note: Paragraphs are first retrieved with the question itself as the query.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: Once the reasoning states an answer or eight steps have passed, a separate run of the language model answers from all collected paragraphs.

chunk.title: Splitting by meaning
chunk.note: The document is split along its structure and the links between paragraphs, so that each fragment is coherent and fits the model window.

align.title: Linking to concepts
align.note: A language model merges duplicates of one entity, assigns each entity to a concept and completes the relations between concepts.

plan.title: Question breakdown
plan.note: The question is broken into subquestions written as logical forms: retrieval, sorting, calculation, deduction.

check.title: Completeness check
check.note: Findings and partial answers go into a shared memory. If the question is not resolved, the model asks a supplementary question and starts a new round.

teacher.title: Teacher scoring
teacher.note: A larger trained model, the teacher, scores how well an English document answers an English question.

align.title: Query-language preference
align.note: Of two equally relevant documents, the one written in the query's language is ranked higher. Relevant documents still stay above irrelevant ones.

candidates.title: First-stage candidates
candidates.note: A first-stage search returns a set of candidate documents, which may be written in several languages.

reranked.title: Final order
reranked.note: Documents are sorted by the new score, and the best ones go to the language model.

bounds.title: Chunk boundaries
bounds.note: An ordinary chunking method marks where each chunk ends, but the text itself is not cut yet.

tokens.title: Token vectors
tokens.note: The model reads the whole document at once, or as much of it as fits, so each token vector reflects all of that text.

index.title: Vector index
index.note: Chunk vectors are stored in an index, and each chunk remembers its document.

knn.title: Nearest chunk search
knn.note: The query vector is compared with the chunk vectors, and the k nearest are taken.

dispatch.title: Choosing the path
dispatch.note: A simple question takes a short path with a small evidence budget; a complex one takes the full path. The path is chosen by rules over the words of the question.

plan.title: Task plan
plan.note: From the question text alone the model drafts a plan: what to observe, how to reason and in what form to answer.

profile.title: Keys and descriptions
profile.note: A language model writes a describing paragraph for every node and every edge; a node is found by its name, an edge by keywords the model adds.

dedup.title: Merging duplicates
dedup.note: Identical entities and relations from different chunks are merged into one node or one edge.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: A language model receives the question together with the descriptions of the found entities and relations and excerpts of the source text.

dag.title: Dependency graph
dag.note: A language model states which subquestion relies on the answer to another. When what is found does not suffice, it adds new subquestions to the graph.

merge.title: Merging subquestions
merge.note: Subquestions of the same rank in the order of resolution are merged into one query.

subanswer.title: Answering a subquestion
subanswer.note: A language model answers the subquestion from the passages found, and the answer conditions retrieval for the subquestions that follow.

answer.title: Final answer
answer.note: A language model composes the final answer from the answers to the subquestions, following the dependency graph.

retrieval.title: Passage retrieval
retrieval.note: The step query is turned into a vector, and the closest passages are found by it.

extract.title: Picking relevant sentences
extract.note: Only the sentences that bear on the step query are taken from the passages found, and they are summarised.

stepanswer.title: Answering the step
stepanswer.note: The answering agent answers the step query from the selected evidence, and the answer joins the history for the next step.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: A language model answers only from the assembled context, and the instruction for the answer depends on the kind of question.

omitted.F1: The paper builds the memory from the whole collection in advance and may save it for reuse, but describes no writing of results back into memory.

extraction.title: Entity and relation extraction
extraction.note: A language model finds in every chunk the entities, the relations between them and the claims about them, and writes a short description of each.

graph.title: Knowledge graph
graph.note: Repeated findings of one entity or relation are merged into one node or one edge, and their descriptions are combined.

prepare.title: Shuffling the reports
prepare.note: The reports of the chosen level are shuffled and divided into portions of a set size.

omitted.A5: The paper describes only the global mode, which uses no vector representations; search by vector closeness belongs to the local mode in the documentation.
omitted.C1: In the global mode of the paper all reports of the chosen level are taken without search; graph traversal belongs only to the local mode in the documentation.

index.title: Vector index
index.note: All image and text pairs are encoded in advance, and their vectors are put into an index for fast search.

query.title: Question
query.note: The question is encoded by the same encoder as the memory.

search.title: Nearest pair search
search.note: The memory entries whose vectors are closest to the vector of the question are found.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The images and texts found are encoded again together with the question, and from them the model writes the answer.

index.title: Vector index
index.note: The vectors of all passages are stored in advance in a fast search library.

q_enc.title: Question encoding
q_enc.note: A separate encoder turns the question into a single vector.

reader.title: Answer extraction
reader.note: A reader model scores the retrieved passages and picks the answer span from the best one.

kg.title: Knowledge graph
kg.note: A ready graph of mental health from an external work links symptoms, conditions and questionnaires.

entry.title: Entry nodes
entry.note: The question is matched against the concepts of the graph. Concepts close enough to it become the starting nodes.

enrichment.title: Query enrichment
enrichment.note: A language model extends the question with related concepts found in the graph.

ranking.title: Graph-aware scoring
ranking.note: A document is scored by the cosine similarity of its vector to the vector of the enriched question, plus a term for its position in the graph.

topk.title: Top-k selection
topk.note: The few documents with the highest score go on.

mapping.title: Ontology mapping
mapping.note: A language model maps the content of the documents onto the entities and attributes of a given ontology and obtains blocks of facts.

flatten.title: Flattening fact blocks
flatten.note: Nested blocks of facts are unfolded into flat sets of key and value pairs without loss of information.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: A language model answers the question from the selected facts.

pipeline.title: Search pipeline with RRF
pipeline.note: A step that fuses results by reciprocal rank is added to the search pipeline.

query.title: Hybrid query
query.note: One query combines several kinds of search and runs through that pipeline.

lexical.title: Keyword search (BM25)
lexical.note: Classic search by word overlap, scored with BM25.

ranks.title: Rank positions
ranks.note: Each document gets its position in the result list of every kind of search.

sort.title: Sorting by fused score
sort.note: The contributions of all lists are added up, and documents are sorted by decreasing sum.

extraction.title: Entity and relation extraction
extraction.note: A language model finds the entities in the text and the relations between them. Each node of the graph holds the name of an entity and the text about it; each edge holds a description of the relation.

mirror.title: Saving the pages
mirror.note: All pages, with their markup, styles and images, are first saved locally so that they can be rendered later without the network.

index.title: Approximate search index
index.note: The vectors of all tiles go into an index that finds close vectors quickly and lets new pages be added without rebuilding it.

answer.title: Answer from the images
answer.note: A model that reads both text and images takes the retrieved tiles as pictures and answers the question.

pool.title: Candidate tag pool
pool.note: For each item, similar items of another popularity class are found and their tags become candidates. The global variant uses one pool of tags for all items.

scoring.title: Tag scoring
scoring.note: A tag scores higher the more often it occurs in the target popularity class compared with the item's own class, and the closer it is in meaning to the item.

tag_edit.title: Editing item tags
tag_edit.note: The attacker changes only the item's tags and leaves the title and genre intact, so the edit stays unnoticed.

item_vectors.title: Item vectors
item_vectors.note: Each item is represented by one embedding vector of its text attributes.

profile.title: User profile
profile.note: The vectors of the items a user interacted with are averaged, weighted by ratings or by recency.

shift.title: Shifted recommendations
shift.note: The aim of the attack: popular items sink in the recommendations and little-known ones rise.

target.title: Choosing the target
target.note: The attacker picks a question and the false answer the system should give to it.

write_text.title: Persuasive text
write_text.note: The attacker's language model writes a short text from which the chosen false answer follows.

check_text.title: Checking the text
check_text.note: A model is asked the question with this text as context. If the answer is not the chosen one, the text is rewritten, up to a set number of trials.

prefix.title: Question-like prefix
prefix.note: The question itself is put before the text so that search finds it. If the retriever is known, the prefix is optimised to bring the text even closer to the question.

inject.title: Injection into the database
inject.note: The attacker adds a few such texts to the knowledge database, for example by editing Wikipedia pages. No access to the system itself is needed.

retrieval.title: Retrieving similar texts
retrieval.note: The system finds the texts closest to the question; the injected texts are built to be among them.

answer.title: Attacker's answer
answer.note: The language model answers from the retrieved texts and gives the answer the attacker chose.

points.title: Points with vectors
points.note: Each point holds a dense, a sparse or several vectors, plus an arbitrary payload.

conditions.title: Payload filter conditions
conditions.note: A query may restrict results by conditions on the payload: keyword match, numeric ranges, geo-location.

omitted.D1: Maximal marginal relevance, which diversifies the results, is offered as an option and is not drawn as a step.

query.title: Query
query.note: The input serves as the query: a caption when an image is to be generated, or an image when a caption is.

search.title: Nearest document search
search.note: The documents whose vectors are closest to the query vector are taken from memory.

diversity.title: Dropping near duplicates
diversity.note: A candidate is skipped when it is too similar to the query or to documents already taken.

prepend.title: Documents before the input
prepend.note: The retrieved documents are placed in front of the input and serve the model as examples.

retrieval.title: Fragment search
retrieval.note: The question and the fragments are turned into vectors, and the fragments closest to the question are taken.

augment.title: One prompt per fragment
augment.note: Each retrieved fragment is placed before the task in a prompt of its own.

mixture.title: Mixing the answers
mixture.note: The language model answers each prompt separately, and the answer probabilities are summed with weights from the search.

lsr.title: Fragment rating
lsr.note: For each fragment the language model computes the probability of the correct answer. The higher it is, the more useful the fragment.

ret_ft.title: Retriever fine-tuning
ret_ft.note: The retriever learns to rank higher the fragments the language model rated as useful. Only the query encoder changes.

know.title: Own knowledge check
know.note: A separately trained model decides whether the language model can answer the question by itself, without search.

retrieve.title: Passage search
retrieve.note: When its own knowledge is not enough, the retriever finds the few most suitable passages in the corpus.

own_answer.title: Own-knowledge answer
own_answer.note: When its knowledge is enough, the language model answers at once and no search is made.

rel_answer.title: Answer from passages
rel_answer.note: When at least one passage is relevant, the language model answers from the relevant passages.

combine.title: Assembling the final answer
combine.note: The language model answers the original question given the subquestions and their answers.

qa.title: Questions and answers
qa.note: Training examples are built from question and answer pairs in the target domain.

docs.title: Document selection
docs.note: The question comes with the document holding the answer and several similar documents without it. In part of the examples the answer document is left out entirely.

topk.title: Document retrieval
topk.note: In use, the documents for a question come from an ordinary search of any kind.

answer.title: Answer of the tuned model
answer.note: The model answers from the retrieved documents, relying on the relevant one and ignoring the rest.

query.title: Query analysis
query.note: Keywords and hints at the wanted kind of content, such as "table" or "figure", are taken from the question, which is then turned into a vector.

semantic.title: Vector similarity search
semantic.note: The question vector is compared with the vectors of all chunks, entities and relations, and the most similar are taken.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The retrieved items are assembled into text, the original images are brought back, and a model that reads text and images writes the answer.

omitted.F1: The paper does not describe how new documents are added to the collection.

synonyms.title: Synonym edges
synonyms.note: The encoder compares the phrases of the graph and links with an edge each pair whose vectors are closer than a threshold.

link.title: Query to triple matching
link.note: The whole question is compared with the triples of the graph by their vectors, and the closest ones are taken.

filter.title: Triple filtering
filter.note: A language model keeps only the retrieved triples that bear on the question.

seeds.title: Seed nodes
seeds.note: Phrases from the kept triples and all passages become seeds. Their scores set the reset probabilities of the walk.

ranking.title: Passage ranking
ranking.note: Passages are ordered by the weight the walk gives them, and the top ones go on.

omitted.F1: The source grows its memory only by adding new texts to the graph and describes no recording of the system's own experience.

search.title: Search for every version
search.note: The original question and every rewrite are searched. Each search yields its own ranked list.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: Only the top documents after reranking reach the model that writes the answer.

embed.title: Vector encoding
embed.note: Every fragment, and later every summary, gets a vector representation.

traversal.title: Tree traversal
traversal.sub: not used in the main runs
traversal.note: At each layer the children of the chosen nodes closest to the question are taken. The main experiments do not use this option.

context.title: Assembling the context
context.note: The texts of the chosen nodes are joined into one context for the answer.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: A ready-made language model answers the question from the assembled text.

entry.title: Starting paragraphs
entry.note: Ten paragraphs from the top documents, closest to the query, are appended to the reply of the ranking tool so that the agent has a place to start.

rerank.title: Reranking matches
rerank.note: A representation model rescores a broad pool of matched lines, and only the best are shown to the agent.

read.title: Reading part of a file
read.note: When a match lacks surrounding context, the agent opens the document and reads only the lines it needs.

answer.title: Agent's answer
answer.note: The agent keeps calling commands until it judges itself ready to answer.

examples.title: Worked examples
examples.note: A few solutions written by people, alternating thoughts, actions and observations, are put into the prompt.

question.title: Question
question.note: The model receives only the question or the claim to check, with no supporting paragraphs.

observation.title: Observation
observation.note: Wikipedia returns the first five sentences of the article, or the next sentence containing the string looked up.

finish.title: Finish with the answer
finish.note: A special action ends the task and gives the answer.

retrieval.title: Document retrieval
retrieval.note: The question and the documents are turned into vectors by one encoder, and the documents closest to the question are taken.

prepend.title: One prompt per document
prepend.note: Each retrieved document is placed before the question, and the language model receives each such prompt separately.

ret_lik.title: Retrieval likelihood
ret_lik.note: The similarity of the documents to the question is turned into a probability distribution over the retrieved documents.

lm_lik.title: Document rating by model
lm_lik.note: The language model stays unchanged. For each document it computes the probability of the correct continuation, and that serves as the document's score.

reindex.title: Index rebuild
reindex.note: Document vectors are recomputed every set number of steps, and training then repeats.

query.title: Question and its type
query.note: Questions are grouped into types by dataset labels or by clustering their vectors.

planner.title: Choosing search settings
planner.note: The retrieval graph supplies the filters that most often led to a correct answer for this type of question, and often rejected passages are excluded.

retrieve.title: Candidate retrieval
retrieve.note: Passages on which the answer may rest are taken from the knowledge base.

reason.title: Answer and verdicts
reason.note: The language model answers and marks each candidate as used or rejected, with a reason.

outcome.title: Outcome check
outcome.note: The signal on whether the answer was correct is added to the decision; profiles later draw only on verdicts from correct answers.

instructions.title: Instruction set
instructions.note: 52 thousand training instructions are taken, with answers written by a strong language model.

search.title: Web and Wikipedia search
search.note: The instruction text is searched with the DuckDuckGo search engine and in Wikipedia. Each example gets zero to three results.

label.title: Labelling the results
label.note: A result is labelled informative when an entailment model judges that it supports the answer, and distracting otherwise.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The model answers relying on the results it has itself named useful.

critic.title: Critic training
critic.note: GPT-4 labels examples with reflection tokens, and a separate critic model is trained on this data.

retrieve.title: Passage search
retrieve.note: An off-the-shelf retriever looks for suitable passages among Wikipedia articles.

relevance.title: Relevance check
relevance.note: The model emits a token saying whether the retrieved passage is relevant.

generate.title: Next segment
generate.note: The model writes the next segment of the answer, relying on the inserted passage.

general_data.title: General-domain training data
general_data.note: General instruction data, question answering over given texts, and examples of writing answers and questions from a document.

stage1.title: First fine-tuning stage
stage1.note: The language model learns to answer from retrieved texts and to draw candidate answers and questions from a document.

corpus.title: Unlabelled domain texts
corpus.note: Documents of a narrow domain with no ready questions and answers.

answers.title: Candidate answer spans
answers.note: The model picks spans of each document that could answer some question.

questions.title: Question generation
questions.note: For each span the model writes a short question or a multiple-choice question; claims to verify are written straight from the document, without a span.

filter.title: Filtering pairs
filter.note: A pair is kept only if its answer occurs in the top documents retrieved for its question.

answer.title: Answer
answer.note: A retriever finds the top texts and the fine-tuned model answers from them.

retrieve.title: Document retrieval
retrieve.note: The question itself serves as the search query to the document base.

cluster.title: Grouping by topic
cluster.note: The retrieved documents are embedded with regard to the question and split into clusters. Each cluster reflects one perspective on the question.

subsets.title: Building subsets
subsets.note: Several subsets are built. Each takes one document from every cluster, so its documents differ in content.

choice.title: Choosing the best draft
choice.note: The draft with the highest final score becomes the answer.

embed.title: Text embedding
embed.note: An embedding model turns the text of each document into a vector.

index.title: One index
index.note: The index stores both the original text of each document and its vector.

keyword.title: Keyword search
keyword.note: Documents are selected by matching the words of the query.

semantic.title: Semantic search
semantic.note: Documents are selected by how close their vectors are to the query vector.

fusion.title: Merging the two lists
fusion.note: The two lists become one, either by the positions of documents in each list or after bringing the scores to a common scale.

ret_orig.title: Retrieval for the original
ret_orig.note: An ordinary search on the question as it was asked.

ret_sb.title: Retrieval for step-back
ret_sb.note: A search for facts about the general concept or principle behind the question.

reasoning.title: Grounded reasoning
reasoning.note: The language model receives the original question and what was found for both questions, and reasons from the general principle to the answer.

context.title: Temporal context
context.note: Details from many frames are combined into a picture of how the event unfolds. Related entities and relations are looked up in the knowledge base, and the most probable entities are kept.

questions.title: Questions for new frames
questions.note: The generator refines the questions using the latest response and sends them to the models with the following frames.

user_query.title: User query
user_query.note: The processor parses the user's query and refines it by the current context and the knowledge base.

serving.title: Retrieval from the graph
serving.note: The serving layer quickly fetches from the graph what the query needs.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: A language model answers from the current state of the graph.

match.title: Node matching
match.note: Names from the search block are matched to graph nodes by the similarity of their vectors.

verbalize.title: Paths as sentences
verbalize.note: The retrieved relations are written as short sentences and inserted into the reasoning. The model goes on and may search again.

omitted.A8: The source takes a ready medical knowledge graph and does not describe how it was built.

topics.title: Topic entities
topics.note: The language model names the main entities of the question, and the paths through the graph start from them.

rel_search.title: Relation search
rel_search.note: For the last entity of each path, all its incoming and outgoing relations are taken from the graph.

rel_prune.title: Relation pruning
rel_prune.note: The language model keeps the few relations most useful for answering the question.

ent_search.title: Entity search
ent_search.note: For each kept relation, the entities at its other end are taken from the graph.

ent_prune.title: Entity pruning
ent_prune.note: The language model keeps the best few entities, and each path grows by one step.

check.title: Path sufficiency check
check.note: The language model decides whether the paths suffice to answer. If not, the search goes on up to a maximum depth.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The model answers from the paths found. If they never sufficed, it answers from its own knowledge.

vocab.title: Vocabulary compression
vocab.note: Words that differ only in case, whitespace or accents are merged into one vocabulary entry.

partition.title: Splitting the vocabulary
partition.note: The vocabulary is split into 16 disjoint groups of similar words of about equal size.

tokens.title: Appending special tokens
tokens.note: Sixteen learnable tokens are appended to the input. Each sees the whole input and is responsible for its own part of the vocabulary.

sparse.title: Sparse word weights
sparse.note: Each special token produces weights over its part of the vocabulary; together the parts form the full sparse vector.

dense.title: Dense vector
dense.note: The dense representation is the hidden state of the end-of-sequence token that precedes the special tokens.

nodes.title: Node selection
nodes.note: A language model finds the names and types of objects in the question, which are then mapped to graph nodes through a reference list.

relations.title: Relation selection
relations.note: A classifier narrows down the relations. Then some relations are picked by vector similarity and some by a language model, and the two lists are merged.

document.title: Long document
document.note: A financial report, legal filing, technical manual or other long, complex professional document.

summaries.title: Node summaries
summaries.note: A language model briefly describes and refines the ready tree, so a basic model is enough here.

reading.title: Reading chosen nodes
reading.note: The model reads only the nodes its reasoning reaches and answers from them.

match.title: Schema and entity matching
match.note: Before the turn ends, matching schemas and entities in both halves of memory are found from the part already transcribed.

left_expand.title: Neighbouring entities
left_expand.note: The matched entities are extended by their nearest neighbours in the graph. The left brain remembers events and entities.

right_expand.title: Traits and attitudes
right_expand.note: Traits and attitudes that match the speech so far are taken, together with the attitudes tied to the entities found by the left brain.

mem_search.title: Search in selected memory
mem_search.note: The search covers only the records attached to the selected nodes, and the results of both brains go into one prompt.

reconcile.title: Reconciling new facts
reconcile.note: After each turn, new facts are extracted and reconciled with nearby records: each is added, updated, deleted or kept.

graph_update.title: Memory graph update
graph_update.note: The schemas, entities and relations used for search are updated.

consolidation.title: Consolidating traits
consolidation.note: After each session, recurring evidence is consolidated into stable traits of the person.

omitted.A3: The paper does not say whether anything beyond the text is attached to stored facts.

embeddings.title: Fragment vectors
embeddings.note: Each fragment is represented in advance by one vector, the same one used for search.

paraphrase.title: Paraphrase pretraining
paraphrase.note: The language model learns to restore a fragment's text from its vector. Only a small bridging network is trained.

instruct.title: Instruction tuning
instruct.note: The bridge is further trained on reading, summarising and question answering grounded in the given fragment, also imitating the model's answers from the full text.

search.title: Fragment search
search.note: The question vector is compared with the fragment vectors, and the single best fragment is taken.

projector.title: Vector projection
projector.note: The bridge maps the vector of the found fragment into the language model's space, so the whole fragment takes one input position instead of its full text of about 180 tokens.

answer.title: Answer generation
answer.note: The model receives the projected vector together with the question. Neither the model nor the search encoder changes.
